citation: Wakabayashi, T., Andrade-Adaniya, F., Schweinhart, L. J., Xiang, Z., Marshall, B. A., & Markley, C. A. (2020). The impact of a supplementary preschool mathematics curriculum on children's early mathematics learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 53, 329-342. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2020.04.002
report_number: Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 53, 329-342; DOI 10.1016/j.ecresq.2020.04.002; IES/NCER grant R305A110483 (Numbers Plus Efficacy Study, PI Lawrence J. Schweinhart, HighScope Educational Research Foundation); WWC study record 90089
design: Multi-site cluster randomized controlled trial (MSCRT) with four nested levels: children within classrooms within sites within states. Randomization performed at the site level within state blocks to reduce contamination (states served as natural blocks; data collected in a different state each year: Michigan Year 1, Maine Year 2, Ohio Year 3). Initial sample: 22 sites, 52 classrooms, 583 children (323 treatment, 260 control). Post-tested sample: 281 treatment, 220 control (501 total; Table 3). TPD intervention = the Numbers Plus supplementary preschool mathematics curriculum (developed by HighScope) layered on the comprehensive whole-child HighScope curriculum, delivered to teachers via professional development: Numbers Plus Training (6 days face-to-face across 2 of 7 modules plus online segments for modules 3-4) followed by ~20 coaching contacts per classroom across the program year (math content/pedagogical-content-knowledge focus; meta-analysis '(P)CK' tag). Comparison = business-as-usual: HighScope curriculum alone, no Numbers Plus (delayed-treatment control; control teachers offered Numbers Plus training after post-data collection). Grade band: Pre-K (4-year-olds). Program types varied by state (for-profit tuition-based PreK in MI; state-funded PreK/Head Start in ME; Head Start in OH). Coded in the meta-analysis as School/center RCT, Pre-k, focus on (P)CK. Both child math achievement outcomes map to STEM.
problems: Only two child math achievement contrasts are reported and only ONE (EMAS) has a fully tabulated multilevel impact estimate (Table 7: Treatment coefficient 0.14, SE 0.06, t=2.34, p<.05). The WJ-III Applied Problems contrast is reported ONLY in prose as a non-significant 'very small effect size (-0.02)' (p. 339, Section 5.2) with NO standard error, no impact table, and no posttest means/SDs -- so its g_var/g_se cannot be computed from the paper. No raw posttest means/SDs are reported for either outcome by treatment arm (Table 5 gives only baseline PQA and pretest scores by state, not posttests). The Table 7 EMAS model is fit on 'Sample: 400 children nested in 22 sites' (per-arm n not broken out per outcome); the per-arm POST-TESTED totals (Table 3) are 281 treatment / 220 control across all three years and are used here as the best available n_t/n_c (the analytic EMAS model n=400 is slightly smaller due to listwise deletion). The WWC study record 90089 (referenced in a prior locked-access placeholder) lists EMAS analytic n=398 and WJ-III n=417; the paper's own Table 7 states n=400 for EMAS, which is used here. The reported effect sizes (0.14 EMAS, -0.02 WJ-III) are model-based standardized treatment coefficients from a 2-level HLM (random intercepts; covariates = corresponding pretest, child age in months, wealth/poverty index, and state dummy variables with Michigan as reference), so they are both pretest-adjusted and cluster-adjusted. Hedges' g equals these values times J (J=0.998 for N~400, negligible). The design-effect ICC is NOT reported anywhere in the paper; cluster_adjusted is true because the impact estimates come from the multilevel model, so an external ICC correction is not needed. NEVER guess the ICC. The Numbers Plus implementation dosage met intended levels (Section 5.1). DISAMBIGUATION (confirmed via the on-disk PDF, not web search): this is the Numbers Plus supplementary-math RCT (a targeted math curriculum + PD layered on the HighScope base, both built by HighScope), NOT the separate AIR/IES 'HighScope Preschool Curriculum and PD Efficacy Study' (R305A150049). The verbatim title, six-author HighScope list, DOI, and math outcomes (WJ-III Applied Problems, EMAS) all match.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Numbers Plus + HighScope (TPD) vs HighScope-alone business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Early Mathematics Assessment System (EMAS) Birthday Party Assessment (Numbers/Operations and Shape/Space/Patterns; 4-year-old continuous form), Ginsburg et al. 2010
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported standardized Treatment coefficient from a 2-level HLM (random intercepts; covariates = EMAS math pretest, child age, wealth/poverty index, state dummies, Michigan reference) treated as d=0.14 (the paper itself labels it 'effect size 0.14'); g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.99811 (df=398, N=400); g = 0.998*0.14 = 0.1397. g_se = J*impact_se = 0.998*0.06 = 0.0599; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.003586. Standardized on the EMAS outcome's SD scale (HLM standardized coefficient). Already accounts for clustering (multilevel model).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 339, Table 7 (Multilevel model for EMAS) and Section 5.2; abstract notes 'small' positive effect on EMAS
effect_sizes.notes: Statistically significant favoring TPD (t=2.34, p<.05). Table 7 sample = 400 children nested in 22 sites (n_t/n_c from Table 3 post-tested totals 281/220 across all 3 years used as best available split; the EMAS model n=400 is slightly smaller due to listwise deletion). EMAS is a developer/researcher-associated instrument (developed at Teachers College/Columbia, Ginsburg et al.; Birthday Party version validated by HighScope-affiliated work) -> labeled researcher_made; central filtering may exclude it as non-independent. Paper: 'the small statistically significant effect size between children exposed to Numbers Plus was 0.14 (p < .05)'. Positive = favors TPD. ICC not reported.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Numbers Plus + HighScope (TPD) vs HighScope-alone business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock-Johnson III Tests of Achievement, Applied Problems (subtest 10), McGrew & Woodcock 2001
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported in prose as a 'very small effect size (-0.02)' from the parallel multilevel impact analysis (pretest-adjusted, cluster-adjusted). g = J*d with J~0.998 (N~400) rounds back to -0.02. No SE/variance computable: the paper provides no WJ-III impact table, no SE, and no posttest means/SDs by arm.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 339, Section 5.2 (Impact on child mathematics outcomes)
effect_sizes.notes: Non-significant ('No significant differences were found for WJ-III Applied Problems, however, with a very small effect size (-0.02)'). WJ-III Applied Problems is a standardized/independent instrument (this is the WWC-eligible math outcome). No multilevel table reported for WJ-III (only EMAS has Table 7), so g_se and g_var cannot be derived from the paper -- impact_se/g_var/g_se left null. The Discussion (Section 6) notes WJ-III may be 'inadequate for the range of mathematical knowledge developing during early childhood', explaining the divergence from the significant EMAS result. Sign is essentially zero/slightly negative (favors control marginally). ICC not reported.
